notes:
Context: large North American 3PL; heavy event-driven ingestion from edge devices + periodic batched analytics. Primary interest is Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and strict latency SLOs for their routing assistant and driver chat features.

Recent summary:
- 2026-02-18: Intro call (AE Maya). CTO Rahul Sharma emphasized need for firm throughput guarantees for peak morning dispatch window. Quote: "We cannot have >200ms tail latency during dispatch spikes."
- 2026-02-28: Infrastructure scoping w/ infra lead (ff_20260228_aurora_scoping). We collected preliminary QPS histogram for last 30 days; peak 18k QPS ingest, steady-state 2.5k QPS (spikes concentrated 05:00-08:30 PST).
- 2026-03-03: Security questionnaire returned; require SOC2 + KMS integration + audit logs + optional air-gap for on-prem staging.
- 2026-03-09: Architectural workshop (ff_20260309_capacity_kickoff). Agreed to run dedicated capacity sizing workshop focused on: baseline QPS, tokens/sec distribution, peak vs steady state planning, reserved GPU pool sizing, autoscale headroom, and SLA terms (SLOs for p50/p95/p99 latency).

Workload specifics / asks:
- Mix: chat (conversational customer support), reranking for carrier selection, embeddings for document search of manifests and invoices, model family preference: Llama-2. Large preference for int8/quantized variants to reduce cost.
- Latency goals: target p95 <= 150ms for short chat turns (~40 tokens), p99 <= 350ms during steady-state; during peak acceptable fallback with degraded model to maintain p99 < 600ms per roadmap.
- Throughput: baseline 2.5k QPS, peak 18k QPS for 45-90 minutes daily; token/sec distribution attached in drive file. Need guidance on token/sec per request and effective token throughput for model selection.
- Reliability/SLA: require 99.95% uptime for Dedicated pool; contractual SLOs for latency and capacity guarantees while allowing fallback to multi-region hosted API for overflow.
- Compliance: data residency for EU customers, audit logs retention 7 years for financial transactions, integration with customer KMS required.

POC / next steps agreed:
1) Redwood to run dedicated sizing workshop (2-hour remote) to propose GPU pool config: reserved GPUs, headroom for autoscale bursts, batching profiles and KV-cache priming approach.
2) Aurora to supply 14 days of anonymized request traces (QPS/time, tokens/request histogram, distribution by route).
3) Engineering follow-up: generate expected tokens/sec baseline and two sizing proposals (cost-optimized and latency-optimized) + draft SLA terms.
4) Procurement to start enterprise contract template review once sizing chosen.

Open negotiation points / blockers:
- Precise definition of capacity failure modes and remedies (what constitutes breach and credit calc).
- Whether on-prem staging environment can be fully air-gapped for SOC audits (Aurora wants a statement of feasibility).
- Cost delta for reserved vs burstable capacity during daily peaks — finance needs model run to justify ARR commitment.

Quick wins:
- Provide initial sizing spreadsheet and cost delta scenarios (requested by 2026-03-15).
- Offer temporary burst capacity on Hosted API while Dedicated pool is provisioned to avoid service disruption during procurement window.
